parole.significato: A Masai ceremony of manhood, involving circumcision.
A Masai ceremony in which a warrior passes into senior warriorhood.
A shamanistic seer and healer among the Maasai people.

Belonging to the earliest widespread stone-tool archaeological industry in prehistory.
parole.testo: From Maasai Olduvai, from the site of Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania, where the first Oldowan lithics were discovered in the 1930s.

parole.significato: A form of spirit possession or spiritual sickness among Maasai people, especially women.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Maasai orpeka, from Swahili upepo (“spirit, wind”), from Proto-Bantu [Term?].
